creator.name: Unknown Neolithic painters of the Horn of Africa

object.medium: ochre, white and black pigment on granite
object.description: Long-horned cows with decorated necks and ceremonial collars, painted in red, white and black on the ceiling of a granite shelter at Laas Geel, outside Hargeisa. The cows are shown with their udders and without legs below the knee, as if seen from the front, and small human figures stand beneath them with their arms raised. The site is among the best preserved rock art in Africa.
facts: Local herders had always known the shelters; a French team recorded them for archaeology in 2002.
There are about twenty painted shelters on the granite outcrop.
Laas Geel means 'the camels' waterhole' in Somali.
